CG1.claim: Chhattisgarh's Bastar region has Chitrakote, India's widest waterfall, and Bastar is known for Dokra metal art.

evidence.quote: the scenic city of Jagdalpur is home to the Chitrakote waterfall, celebrated as the widest waterfall in India
Don't miss the exquisite Dokra artworks on display

CG2.claim: The Hareli festival, named for greenery, celebrates the farming year; the Bastar Dussehra at Jagdalpur lasts 75 days.

evidence.quote: The Hareli festival, a celebration, that derives its name from 'Haryali,' meaning greenery in Hindi
partake in the vibrant Bastar Dussehra or Jagdalpur Dussehra. Lasting for 75 da

CG_AIR.claim: Swami Vivekananda Airport is about 15 km south-east of Raipur.

evidence.quote: The airport is located at Mana, about 15 km (9.3 mi) south-east of Raipur

RPR1.claim: Raipur, the capital, has the Nandanvan Zoo and Safari with over 700 animals; Ghatarani, the state's largest waterfall, is 85 km away. Visit November to February.

evidence.quote: Nandanvan Zoo and Safari is a must-visit, home to over 700 animals
a day trip to Ghatarani Waterfalls, 85 km from Raipur, is an unforgettable experience. As the largest waterfall in Chhattisgarh
The best time to visit Raipur is during the winter, from November to February

JAG1.claim: Jagdalpur is the heart of tribal Bastar; its Anthropological Museum shows the region's indigenous cultures.

evidence.quote: Jagdalpur, is the urban heart of the tribal Bastar region in Chhattisgarh
Start your exploration at the acclaimed Anthropological Museum

JAG2.claim: Jagdalpur is about 320 km from Visakhapatnam airport and 270 km (about six hours) from Raipur; trains include the Hirakhand and Araku Express.

evidence.quote: The nearest major airport is Visakhapatnam Airport which is around 320 km away.
It takes six hours to cover the 270 kilometers that connect Jagdalpur and Ra
You can take the Hirakhand Express or Araku Express from Visakhapatnam.

CHT1.claim: Chitrakote, 38 km from Jagdalpur, is India's widest waterfall — nearly 300 m across in the monsoon — where the Indravati drops 30 m.

evidence.quote: Located 38 kilometres from Jagdalpur in the Bastar district
Stretching nearly 300 metres (980 ft.) during the monsoon season, this is the state’s largest, most water-logged and India’s widest waterfall.
It takes a heart-stopping 30-metre (98 ft.) plunge

KNG1.claim: Kanger Valley National Park, declared in 1982, covers 200 sq km with 150 bird species including the Bastar hill myna; open 8 am–5 pm except Tuesdays.

evidence.quote: Declared a National Park in 1982, this expansive 200 square kilometre protected area
Boasting over 300 plant species, 150 bird species and 35 mammals
Opening time - 08:00 AM
Except Tuesday's

KOT1.claim: The Kotumsar caves, about 40 km from Jagdalpur, run over 2 km underground through five chambers; open 8 am–5 pm.

evidence.quote: Travel approximately 40 kilometres from Jagdalpur
The cave system extends over two kilometres underground
There are five chambers
Opening time - 08:00 AM

BSP1.claim: Bastar Palace in Jagdalpur was the royal residence of the Bastar rulers; open 8 am–6 pm.

evidence.quote: It served as the primary residence of the royal family and a centre for administrative activities.
Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM

DNG1.claim: Dongargarh's Bambleshwari Temple sits atop a 1,600-foot hill; a 30-foot Buddha stands on Pragyagiri.

evidence.quote: the magnificent Bambleshwari Temple perched atop a 1,600-foot hill
an impressive 30-foot Buddha statue on Pragyagiri Hill

JH1.claim: Jharkhand is home to the Baidyanath Jyotirlinga at Deoghar and to waterfalls like Hundru, which drops 98 m.

evidence.quote: Jharkhand is home to one of the 12 Jyotirlingas known as Baidyanath Temple located in Deogarh.
These falls are a natural wonder formed by the Subarnarekha River, plunging from a remarkable height of 98 metres

JH2.claim: Jharkhand's tribal calendar begins with Rohini, marking the sowing season.

evidence.quote: Among these celebrations, Rohini emerges as one of the earliest, marking the commencement of the agricultural season

RAN1.claim: Ranchi's Birsa Munda Airport is about 7 km from the centre, with flights to Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai.

evidence.quote: Birsa Munda Airport, located about 7 km from the city center, operates regular flights to and from major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, and Mumbai.

RAN2.claim: Ranchi is known for waterfalls — Hundru plunges over 300 feet.

evidence.quote: Among these natural wonders, the Hundru Falls demands a special mention. Plummeting from a height of over 300 feet

DAS1.claim: Dassam Falls near Ranchi, where the Kanchi river drops about 44 m, is at its best July to September.

evidence.quote: The waterfall, also known as Dassam Ghagh, plunges from a height of about 44 meter
The best time to visit Dassam Falls is during the monsoon season, from July to September

DEO1.claim: Deoghar, on the Mayurakshi about 240 km from Ranchi, is Jharkhand's most sacred site; the Naulakha Mandir and Trikut hill's ropeway are nearby.

evidence.quote: This holy city, roughly 240 km from Ranchi, is revered as Jharkhand's most sacred site
Visit the beautiful Naulakha Mandir
soar through the skies on the ropeway

BAI1.claim: Baba Baidyanath Dham is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas; the main 72-foot temple stands among 22 temples.

evidence.quote: It is one of the twelve revered Jyotirlingas – sacred shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva.
At 72 feet tall, it's the largest among a complex of 22 temples

BAI2.claim: During the monsoon Shrawani Mela, pilgrims carry Ganga water 108 km from Sultanganj to the temple.

evidence.quote: During the monsoon festival of Shrawani Mela, devotees embark on a remarkable pilgrimage.
Imagine a line of faithful stretching 108 kilometres, all carrying holy water from the river Ganga in Sultanganj

BET1.claim: Betla National Park, about 232 sq km, was once the Palamau Wildlife Sanctuary; it records over 200 bird species and is open 5 am–7 pm.

evidence.quote: Encompassing an area of approximately 232 square kilometres
Originally known as the Palamau Wildlife Sanctuary
with over 200 species of birds recorded within its boundaries
Opening time - 05:00 AM

BET2.claim: Nearby are Netarhat, the 'Queen of Chotanagpur', and the 16th-century Palamau Fort.

evidence.quote: Netarhat Plateau, known as the "Queen of Chotanagpur,"
Palamau Fort, a historic site dating back to the 16th century

HAZ1.claim: Hazaribagh Wildlife Sanctuary covers 184 sq km of hills and valleys, with 111 km of safari roads; open 6 am–8 pm.

evidence.quote: explore 184 square kilometres of
Take part in exhilarating jeep safaris along well-maintained roads of 111 kilometres
Opening time - 06:00 AM

JAM1.claim: Jamshedpur, India's 'Steel City', was founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907; Tatanagar junction links it to major cities. Visit October to February.

evidence.quote: Jamshedpur, often hailed as the Steel City of India
Founded by the visionary industrialist Jamsetji Tata in 1907
The best time to visit Jamshedpur is during the winter months from October to February

DAL1.claim: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, 30 km from Jamshedpur, was set up in 1975 to protect elephants and covers about 195 sq km of hills.

evidence.quote: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, which is just 30 kilometres from the city of Jamshedpur
Established in 1975 to protect the resident elephants and other fauna, the sanctuary spans an area of approximately 195 square kms.

HR1.claim: Haryana runs from the Shivalik Hills to the Aravallis; its festivals include Teej and Gita Jayanti.

evidence.quote: from the Shivalik Hills in the northeast to the Aravalli Range in the south
From the colourful festivities of Teej, Guga Navmi, Gita Jayanti

HR2.claim: Panchkula's Cactus Garden, with over 3,500 species, is Asia's largest; Morni Hills is 45 km from Chandigarh.

evidence.quote: Encompassing a staggering variety of over 3,500 species of cacti, the Cactus Garden in Panchkula stands as Asia's largest sanctuary
Situated a mere 45 kilometres from Chandigarh

KUR1.claim: Kurukshetra is known as the battlefield of the Mahabharata; at Jyotisar, Krishna is said to have delivered the Bhagavad Gita.

evidence.quote: This city in Haryana is famously known as the site of the epic battle of Mahabharata.
Nearby, the Jyotisar is revered as the place where Lord Krishna delivered the sacred Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna.

KUR2.claim: Visit October to March; Chandigarh airport is about 100 km away, Delhi's about 160 km.

evidence.quote: The best time to visit Kurukshetra is during the winter months, from October to March.
the nearest major airport is the Chandigarh Airport, which is 100 kilometres away

KUR3.claim: Kurukshetra's Bhadrakali Temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.

evidence.quote: Another significant temple is the Bhadrakali Temple , one of the 51 Shakti peeths dedicated to Kali.

PNP1.claim: Panipat, about 90 km north of Delhi on the Grand Trunk Road, saw three decisive battles; Babur's Kabuli Bagh Mosque of 1527 marks the start of Mughal architecture.

evidence.quote: On the historic Grand Trunk Road, about 90 km north of Delhi, lies Panipat
The First Battle of Panipat (1526)  saw Babur defeat Ibrahim Lodi
Built by Babur in 1527 after his victory in the First Battle of Panipat, Kabuli Bagh Mosque marks the beginning of Mughal architecture in India.

PNP2.claim: Panipat is known as the 'City of Weavers'; Ibrahim Lodi's tomb and Hemu's memorial are here.

evidence.quote: Known as the “City of Weavers”
His tomb stands quietly in Panipat

SUL1.claim: Sultanpur National Park near Gurugram is a bird sanctuary with over 250 species.

evidence.quote: a bird sanctuary that is home to over 250 species of birds

CH1.claim: Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier on a grid of sectors; its Capitol Complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: Envisioned by the renowned Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier, Chandigarh offers a unique grid-like design
At the forefront is the Capitol Complex, a UNESCO World Heritage site that epitomises modernist architecture.

CH2.claim: Chandigarh has over 100 heritage trees; Leisure Valley runs through the city.

evidence.quote: Over 100 majestic heritage trees stand tall as silent witnesses to the city's history.

ROC1.claim: Nek Chand, a road inspector, began the Rock Garden in secret in 1957; it opened in 1976 and spreads over 40 acres with over 5,000 statues made from waste.

evidence.quote: Crafted by a former road inspector, Nek Chand, in 1957
Spread across a massive 40-acre wonderland
With over 5,000 statues adorning its borders
In 1976, the gates to this enchanting realm were opened.

CAP1.claim: Le Corbusier's Capitol Complex spreads over 100 acres with the Assembly, Secretariat and High Court, and the 85-foot Open Hand Monument.

evidence.quote: The imposing Capitol Complex spreads over 100 acres and comprises three significant buildings: the seat of the Legislative Assembly, the Secretariat Building, and the High Court.
Marvel at the 85-foot-high Open Hand sculpture
UNESCO World Heritage Site in Chandigarh capital region, India

SUK1.claim: Sukhna, a 3 sq km rain-fed lake below the Shivaliks created in 1958, bans motorboats; open 5 am–9 pm with boating year-round.

evidence.quote: A declared National Wetland, this 3 square kilometre rain-fed reservoir came into existence in 1958
motorboats are forbidden on the water
Opening time - 05.00 AM
Boating, rowing, sculling, sailing, kayaking, and water-skiing are available year-round.

ROS1.claim: The Zakir Hussain Rose Garden, set up in 1967, is Asia's largest — 30 acres with 50,000 rose bushes.

evidence.quote: Established in 1967, Asia’s largest rose garden spans over 30 acres and boasts an incredible collection of 50,000 rose bushes

evidence.quote: 112 is now the pan-country single emergency number for all emergencies.

Applicant's passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa.
